domains_and_motifs.name: Tankyrase-binding domain
domains_and_motifs.description: N-terminal domain responsible for tankyrase (TNKS1/TNKS2) binding. Contains the tankyrase-binding motif (TBM) that mediates TNKS interaction leading to PARsylation and subsequent proteasomal degradation of AXIN1

domains_and_motifs.name: RGS domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Regulator of G-protein Signaling domain homologous to RGS proteins. This domain is needed for APC binding through interaction with SAMP repeats. The RGS domain is a structured, folded domain that mediates critical protein-protein interactions in the beta-catenin destruction complex

domains_and_motifs.name: CK1α phosphorylation motif
domains_and_motifs.description: N-terminal casein kinase 1 alpha (CK1α) consensus phosphorylation motif. Multiple serine/threonine residues including S51, S54, T56, S57, T58 and T60 are phosphorylated by CK1α. This phosphorylation occurs within the tankyrase-binding site and counteracts tankyrase-mediated degradation

sources.notes: Phosphorylation at N-terminal CK1 site identified through mass spectrometry and functional studies

domains_and_motifs.name: GSK3β binding region
domains_and_motifs.description: Central intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that contains the binding site for GSK3β. This region brings GSK3β into proximity with substrates like beta-catenin for phosphorylation. The region is largely unstructured and facilitates dynamic scaffold assembly

sources.notes: Central region binds GSK3beta and beta-catenin
Central IDR characterized in structural and functional studies

domains_and_motifs.name: Beta-catenin binding domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Region within the central IDR that mediates binding to beta-catenin (CTNNB1). This binding site allows AXIN1 to position beta-catenin near GSK3β for sequential phosphorylation, marking it for ubiquitination and degradation

domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear localization signal 1
domains_and_motifs.description: First nuclear localization signal sequence that directs AXIN1 import into the nucleus

domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear export signal
domains_and_motifs.description: Nuclear export signal sequence that directs AXIN1 export from the nucleus to the cytoplasm

domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear localization signal 2
domains_and_motifs.description: Second nuclear localization signal sequence overlapping with the NES region

domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear localization signal 3
domains_and_motifs.description: Third nuclear localization signal sequence near the C-terminus

domains_and_motifs.name: Multi-protein interaction region
domains_and_motifs.description: Region implicated in interactions with various proteins including C9orf140, RNF111, HIPK2, and MEKK4

sources.notes: Peptide microarray study identified this region

domains_and_motifs.name: DIX domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Dishevelled and Axin (DIX) domain located at the C-terminus. This domain mediates homodimerization of AXIN1 molecules and heterodimerization with Dishevelled (DVL) proteins through head-to-tail polymerization interfaces. Critical for AXIN1 self-assembly and interaction with the Wnt pathway activator DVL

experimental_structures.description: Crystal structure of the RGS-homologous domain of AXIN from Homo sapiens
Crystal structure of AXIN DIX domain from Rattus norvegicus (highly homologous to human)
Beta-catenin binding domain of Axin in complex with beta-catenin
Complex structure of Axin-DIX and Dvl2-DIX showing heterodimeric interaction

alphafold_prediction.confidence_summary: Global pLDDT: 62.3. High confidence (pLDDT > 90) for structured RGS and DIX domains. Low to very low confidence (pLDDT ≤ 50) for intrinsically disordered regions in the N-terminal IDR and central IDR (aa 212-779)

post_translational_modifications.function: Regulates interaction with gamma-tubulin and prevents excessive centrosome generation
Facilitates AXIN1 liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) formation
Marks AXIN1 for proteasomal degradation following tankyrase-mediated PARsylation
Poly-ADP-ribosylation by tankyrases (TNKS1/2) within N-terminal domain, prerequisite for ubiquitination and degradation
Required for activation of the JNK pathway

function.uniprot_function: Component of the beta-catenin destruction complex required for regulating CTNNB1 levels through phosphorylation and ubiquitination in the absence of Wnt signaling. Scaffolding protein that brings together GSK3B, CK1, APC, and beta-catenin to facilitate sequential phosphorylation of beta-catenin, marking it for degradation. Functions as a tumor suppressor by negatively regulating the Wnt signaling pathway. Also participates in the AXIN1-HIPK2-TP53 complex which controls cell growth, apoptosis, and development. Recently identified as boosting antiviral response through IRF3 stabilization and induced phase separation
function.tissue_specificity: Widely expressed with particularly high expression in adult heart, skeletal muscle, and kidney

biological_process.term: negative regulation of Wnt signaling pathway
G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

reactome.pathway_name: Degradation of beta-catenin by the destruction complex

kegg.pathway_name: Signaling pathways regulating pluripotency of stem cells

pathways.pathway_role_summary: AXIN1 is a central scaffold protein in the beta-catenin destruction complex, functioning as a negative regulator of canonical Wnt signaling. It brings together GSK3β, CK1α, APC, and beta-catenin to facilitate sequential phosphorylation of beta-catenin, marking it for BTRC-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. AXIN1 also participates in Hippo, MAPK, mTOR, AMPK, TGFβ, and antioxidant signaling pathways, and has recently been identified in antiviral responses through IRF3 stabilization. Regulated by tankyrase-mediated PARsylation and RNF146-mediated ubiquitination, AXIN1 levels control Wnt pathway activity

disease_associations.description: Biallelic mutations that abrogate AXIN1 expression or result in truncated proteins have been identified in hepatocellular carcinomas, leading to activated Wnt signaling
Deletion, missense and nonsense mutations in AXIN1 gene lead to activated WNT signaling in colorectal cancers
AXIN1 mutations identified in medulloblastoma tumors result in loss of tumor suppressor function
AXIN1 mutations associated with developmental defects

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive data available from multiple sources. Quantitative kinetic data (Kd values) available for some interactions (GSK3B, TNKS) but limited for others (APC, CTNNB1, DVL2). PTM sites extensively characterized by mass spectrometry. Structural data available for RGS domain, DIX domain, and beta-catenin binding region. Central IDR lacks high-resolution structure but characterized functionally. Some interaction partners lack detailed binding site mapping and quantitative affinity measurements
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: AXIN1 is critical for Wnt pathway modeling as the rate-limiting scaffold of the beta-catenin destruction complex. Its regulated degradation by tankyrases and stabilization by CK1α/USP7 creates dynamic control over Wnt signaling. The availability of Kd values for GSK3B (7.5 nM) and TNKS (0.92 μM), along with enzymatic parameters (KM changes), enables quantitative modeling. AXIN1's intrinsically disordered regions and capacity for liquid-liquid phase separation add complexity to modeling its scaffold function. Key for understanding switch-like Wnt pathway responses and disease mutations
